summary: Telegram-driven remote shell with command-encoding anti-forensics
details: Package advertises itself as a Telegram bot for 'remote VPS management' and installs a CLI entry point (httpz-requests = httpz_requests.cli:main) that starts a bot polling api.telegram.org for messages and executes those messages as shell commands on the host running the bot, returning output back over Telegram. This is a network-to-shell dataflow: remote Telegram users drive arbitrary command execution on the machine running the tool. The runtime is shipped exclusively as Cython-compiled.so files (no Python source), and a dedicated obfuscate module exposes enc_b64 and _xor helpers used by core/handlers; the README explicitly states that commands are executed in encoded form so they do not appear in plaintext in the process list or logs — anti-forensics engineering paired with the remote-shell function. Publisher metadata is placeholder: author name 'Aapka Naam', author-email 'you@example.com', and Homepage/Repository URLs containing the literal 'YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME' — no accountability channel for the maintainer of a remote-shell tool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
